name: ESSAI 2026
venue: European Summer School on Artificial Intelligence, Vienna, Austria
description: The 2026 European Summer School on Artificial Intelligence (ESSAI) takes place in Vienna, Austria from 6 to 10 July. It offers a one‑week program of introductory and advanced AI courses, specialized tutorials on Bilateral AI and Digital Humanism, and six parallel tracks taught by over 30 international lecturers. The school also provides networking opportunities and a social program, including a reception at the Vienna City Hall, aimed at PhD students and young researchers.

name: OpenEuroLLM Winter School
description: The 2026 Winter School on Multilinguality in LLM Development and Evaluation is organized by the Nordic Language Processing Laboratory and the University of Oslo in Norway. It targets NLP researchers, especially those from EuroHPC consortium countries and doctoral students, offering in‑depth technical presentations, hands‑on elements and discussions on multilingual large language models. The event is held at the Skeikampen conference hotel north of Oslo, includes subsidized participation, group bus transfers from Oslo Airport, and provides meals and accommodation options.

name: Probabilistic AI School
description: ProbAI School 2026 is a Probabilistic AI School taking place in Vilnius, Lithuania. The programme aims to provide an inclusive educational environment featuring state‑of‑the‑art expertise in machine learning and artificial intelligence. It welcomes enthusiasts, students, academics, and industry professionals to participate in the five‑day event.

name: BMVA Computer Vision Summer School
venue: Robert Gordon University, Aberdeen, Scotland, United Kingdom
description: The 30th BMVA Computer Vision Summer School will be held at Robert Gordon University in Aberdeen, Scotland. It offers an intensive week of lectures and lab sessions covering a wide range of topics in computer vision, delivered by leading researchers from the UK and abroad. The five‑day programme features daily oral talks and hands‑on sessions designed for students and early‑career researchers seeking advanced training in the field.

name: Oxford Machine Learning Summer School 2026
venue: Oxford Machine Learning School, Oxford, United Kingdom
description: OxML 2026 was a machine‑learning school organized by the Oxford Machine Learning School, offering three advanced programmes in online and hybrid formats. The programmes covered building AI models from scratch (MLx Cases), applications of representation learning and generative AI to health and biomedicine (MLx Health & Bio), and the latest advances in representation learning, foundation and frontier models (MLx Representation Learning & Gen AI). Participants engaged with leading researchers, worked on hands‑on projects, and could access recordings and materials through the Elandi learning dashboard after the event.

name: Robotics, Perception and Learning (RPL) Summer School
venue: KTH Royal Institute of Technology, Stockholm, Sweden
description: The RPL Summer School 2026 is a six‑day event for doctoral and postdoctoral researchers focusing on robotics, perception and learning. It covers topics such as machine learning, computer vision, robotics, human‑robot interaction, planning and decision making, and combines keynote talks, industry panels, brainstorming sessions and student presentations. Held at the Happy Tammsvik resort in Stockholm, the school aims to foster new collaborations by providing a relaxed setting with indoor and outdoor activities.

name: Machine Learning Crash Course at MALGA
description: The MLCC2026 Summer School – Machine Learning Crash Course – provides an introduction to fundamental machine‑learning concepts and algorithms. It is aimed at undergraduate and graduate students, as well as professionals, and is open to participants from any university after a selection process. The five‑day in‑person program in Genoa combines theoretical lectures with hands‑on lab sessions and includes a final test consisting of notebook work and a report.

name: UK Robotics Summer School
venue: National Robotarium, Heriot-Watt University, Edinburgh, United Kingdom
description: The UK Robotics Summer School is a five‑day program held at the National Robotarium, Heriot‑Watt University in Edinburgh, United Kingdom. It offers expert‑led lectures, tutorials, industry talks and hands‑on experience with state‑of‑the‑art robotics technology, focusing on cutting‑edge topics in the field. The school targets master’s‑level students and industry practitioners, providing networking opportunities with academics and industry leaders.

name: International Summer School for Advanced Studies on Biometrics, Behavior, and Vision
description: The 2027 Biometrics Summer School takes place at Hotel Dei Pini in Porto Conte near Alghero, Sardinia, Italy. It focuses on the impact of agentic AI and vision foundation models on biometrics and human recognition, covering topics such as machine learning, image understanding, signal analysis, neuroscience, robotics, and digital forensics. The program is aimed at PhD students, post‑docs, researchers, forensic examiners and professionals, offering lectures by 18 international experts, hands‑on sessions, and the possibility of scholarships and a videoconference option.

name: Winter School on Ethical, Legal, and Societal (ELS) aspects of AI and AS at Umeå University
description: The Winter School on Ethical, Legal, and Societal (ELS) aspects of AI and AS is announced. It focuses on exploring the ethical, legal, and societal implications of artificial intelligence and autonomous systems. Materials and projects related to the school are hosted on GitHub.

name: Winter School on Social Robotics, Artificial Intelligence and Multimedia (SoRAIM 2026)
description: The ACM Europe Winter School SoRAIM’27 focuses on social robotics, artificial intelligence, and multimedia. It targets PhD students and early‑career researchers, offering lectures, hands‑on sessions, and informal networking in a mountain setting. The venue in Escandille, Autrans, in the Vercors mountains near Grenoble provides opportunities for outdoor activities and interdisciplinary collaboration.

name: Northern Lights Deep Learning Winter School
venue: UiT The Arctic University of Norway, Tromsø, Norway
description: The Winter School is part of the Northern Lights Deep Learning Conference 2027 in Tromsø, Norway. It runs from 11 to 15 January 2027 and focuses on deep learning topics such as image classification, object detection, segmentation, time series prediction and speech recognition. The event is hosted by UiT The Arctic University of Norway and offers researchers opportunities to exchange ideas, collaborate, and learn from leading experts.

name: Annual Nepal AI School (ANAIS)
description: The 7th Annual Nepal AI School (ANAIS) is an 11‑day intensive in‑person program held at Kathmandu World School in Kathmandu, Nepal. It offers lectures, labs, and project work covering fundamentals to advanced topics such as geometric deep learning, world models, generative modeling, and neuro‑symbolic AI, targeting senior undergraduates, graduate students, PhD candidates, faculty, and industry professionals. The school aims to foster collaboration among international researchers and inspire early‑stage researchers from Nepal and the region to tackle high‑impact AI problems.

name: EEML Summer School
description: The Eastern European Machine Learning Summer School takes place in Cetinje, Montenegro from 27 July to 1 August 2026. It offers an intensive program of lectures and tutorials on modern machine‑learning research presented by leading experts from academia and industry across Europe and the United States. The school is aimed at graduate students and early‑career researchers who want to deepen their knowledge and build collaborations within the Eastern European AI community.

name: Mediterranean Summer School
venue: Mediterranean Machine Learning Summer School, Barcelona, Spain
description: The Mediterranean Machine Learning (M2L) Summer School is a five‑day program held in Barcelona, Spain, offering keynotes, lectures, and practical sessions led by international AI experts. It targets doctoral and outstanding master students, academics, and practitioners, focusing on topics such as computer vision, natural language processing, generative and diffusion models, reinforcement learning, and ethics in machine learning. The school emphasizes diversity, networking, and collaboration through poster sessions, scholarships, and cultural activities.

name: AthNLP Summer School 2026
description: The Athens Natural Language Processing Summer School 2026 is a week‑long program held at the NCSR Demokritos campus in Athens, Greece. It brings together experts from RC Athena, NCSR Demokritos, Athens University of Economics and Business, Heriot‑Watt University, the Archimedes Unit, and ELLIS‑University of Manchester to deliver lectures and hands‑on sessions on modern NLP techniques. The school targets graduate students and early‑career researchers interested in state‑of‑the‑art language models, offering networking opportunities and a link to the subsequent EETN AI conference.

name: Advanced Artificial Intelligence: GenAI & Deep Unsupervised Learning
venue: Lady Margaret Hall, Oxford, United Kingdom
description: The AI For Finance summer school is a three‑week residential or online programme offered by Lady Margaret Hall, Oxford. It explores how artificial intelligence techniques such as neural networks, time‑series forecasting, reinforcement learning and agentic AI are applied to quantitative finance, risk management, trading and investment research. The course is aimed at students and aspiring finance professionals who want to gain practical skills in AI‑driven financial modelling and understand the limitations and risks of frontier technologies.

name: LUT Summer School
description: LUT Summer School is a one‑week intensive program that offers courses on sustainability, climate action, marketing, management and the intersection of business and technology. It is aimed at bachelor’s and master’s students from any university, combining online instruction with a on‑campus week at the Lappeenranta campus in August 2027. The programme also includes a social programme featuring Finnish nature experiences, sauna evenings and other cultural activities.

name: 1st Internationa School on the Cognitive, Ethical, and Societal Dimensions of AI - AIces
description: The AIces 2026 International School on the Cognitive, Ethical and Societal Dimensions of Artificial Intelligence takes place in Porto, Portugal from 30 March to 2 April 2026. It offers multidisciplinary training for graduate students, postgraduate students and industry practitioners, with parallel courses, a symposium, and open‑debate sessions covering cognition, ethics and society. Participants can attend in person or online, receive recorded lectures for 45 days, and obtain a certificate that may be used for ECTS recognition.

name: Summer School on Multimodal Foundation Models and Generative AI
venue: Institut National des Postes et Télécommunications, Rabat, Morocco
description: The 2nd edition of the AI Summer School on Multimodal Foundation Models and Generative AI is a five‑day immersive program jointly organized by MoroccoAI, INPT, IMT Nord Europe, and Soft Centre. It targets master, Ph.D., post‑doc, and early‑career researchers as well as industry professionals, offering expert lectures, hands‑on labs, and project mentorship on state‑of‑the‑art AI research. The school takes place at the Institut National des Postes et Télécommunications in Rabat, providing participants with both cutting‑edge technical training and networking opportunities across Morocco’s AI ecosystem.

name: AI4Science Summer School
description: The 2nd Summer School on Advancing Scientific Discovery with AI brings together researchers, PhD students and post‑doctoral scholars to explore AI methods for accelerating scientific research. The program covers machine learning for data analysis, AI‑driven experimental design, generative models, and integration of AI with physical simulations, featuring hands‑on workshops and case studies. Participants are expected to have experience with Python, NumPy and PyTorch, and will work on practical projects to apply AI techniques to their own scientific domains.
